sam: Quick smoke test dump for KV prefix priming + kernel selection under concurrency. Posting raw notes + short logs. cc @maria @kai :mag:

oliver: Thanks — can you outline the harness and config? want to reproduce locally.

sam: Repro command i used:
```
./replay_harness \
  --trace=/replays/prefix_hotspot_20260318.trace \
  --concurrency=64 \
  --target-qps=1200 \
  --kernel-mode=auto \
  --kv-cache-size=8GB \
  --prefix-priming=true \
  --batching=adaptive
```

sam: TL;DR results (30s warmup + 10m run):
- priming=true: hit-rate 87% @60s, 92% steady @10m, p50=14ms, p95=78ms, throughput=980 req/s
- priming=false: hit-rate 42% @60s, 61% steady @10m, p50=22ms, p95=210ms, throughput=720 req/s
- kernel-mode=auto vs kernel-mode=force-wmma: auto gave ~6% better p95 on long seqs due to dynamic kernel pick

maria: Those hit-rate deltas are large. did you control for trace ordering? synthetic vs replay?

sam: Yep — this is replay (hotspot trace). I ran 3 seeds (replay ids: 20260318-primingY, 20260318-primingN, 20260318-primingY-rerun). Synthetic tests (zipf) gave similar direction but smaller gaps: priming helps ~+18% hit-rate.

kai: Any evidence of eviction churn or correctness issues under high concurrency?

sam: Saw eviction bursts correlated with p95 spikes. Grep from runtime log (abridged):
```
[12:03:15] WARN kv_cache: eviction spike shard=3 evicted=1024 latency_ms=32 lock_wait_ms=8
[12:03:15] WARN runtime:batchesize: adaptive oscillation -> 1->64->8 cycles
[12:03:16] ERROR kv_cache: stale-prefix-read detected key=prefix_xxx seq=243 expected=238
```
small note: stale-prefix-read happened twice across 9 runs; both when priming=false and concurrency>=48. We suspect a race where eviction clears KV while request is in-progress and the prefetch callback reads a removed entry.

oliver: That's worrying — do we have a repro that triggers the stale read deterministically?

sam: Not fully deterministic yet. Steps to repro: increase concurrency to 128, lower kv-cache-size to 4GB to force evictions, use the hotspot trace. I can attach a minimal harness script.

maria: On batching heuristics — you mentioned oscillation. Is adaptive batching sampling throughput/latency and changing batch_size? Any logs to show policy decisions?

sam: Yes, adaptive policy uses a smoothed P50 and queue depth to pick power-of-two batches. When eviction latency spikes, the controller sees higher tail latencies and drops batch size; that reduces batching efficiency and increases QoS variance. Example controller log lines:
```
[controller] sample: qd=12 p50=18ms -> batch=32
[controller] sample: qd=3 p50=86ms -> batch=4
[controller] sample: qd=20 p50=16ms -> batch=64
```

kai: Kernel selection note — auto mode queries model-seq histogram and chooses kernels per-layer. Did you pin kernel to test apples-to-apples?

sam: I ran both: auto vs forced (force-wmma). Auto chooses faster kernel for short sequences, wmma for long. For apples-to-apples we should fix kernel-mode and match batch config. The short smoke above compared auto vs force-wmma and auto was better on our mixed length trace.

maria: For the KV correctness angle, can we instrument the cache to add a per-op generation counter and assert during reads? Might help catch stale reads with stack traces.

sam: Good idea. I added a quick assert in the priming path to log the owner-thread and generation. It doubles the write cost but for debug runs it caught the race once with stack. I'll push a small patch to my branch sam/kv-priming-trace.

perf-bot: Benchmark summary uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/1769994321 (priming smoke). Summary: primingY: 92% hit steady, p95=78ms; primingN: 61% hit steady, p95=210ms.

oliver: Next steps?

sam: Propose:
1) reproduce stale-prefix-read deterministically (concurrency=128, smaller cache) and capture stack traces.
2) try per-shard eviction + background async eviction to reduce lock hold times.
3) run apples-to-apples runs with kernel pinned to avoid confounding kernel selection.
4) re-run with deterministic seeds and attach perf-bot comparisons.

maria: +1 — i'll own 2) with infra. kai can help instrument. oliver pls run kernel-pinned apples. sam plz add the harness script and config to PR.

kai: I'll add generation counters to instrument reads and add an opt-in flag to avoid perf impact in normal runs.

sam: attached minimal harness snippet (will push to PR):
```
# minimal reproduce
for c in 32 64 96 128; do
  ./replay_harness --trace=... --concurrency=$c --kv-cache-size=4GB --prefix-priming=false &
done
```

oliver: OK i'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to triage. Anyone object?

maria: nope :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all. I'll tag updates here when I have a deterministic repro.

perf-bot: auto:compare: 1769994321 vs baseline 1769000000 -> primingY shows 28% better throughput, 63% lower p95 on hotspot trace.

sam: filing follow-up issue: infra/kv-priming-eviction-race (will include logs + replay ids).
